summary: Roger T. Ames is a scholar in philosophy and sinology. He earned his BA at the University of British Columbia, an MA at National Taiwan University, and a PhD at SOAS under D. C. Lau, serving at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1978–2016).

Roland Barthes was a French philosopher and linguist who studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand, Lycée Montaigne, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Émile Benveniste. His career included posts at CNRS (~1952–1959), EHESS (~1962–1976), and Collège de France (1976–1980).
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. He held an assistant professorship at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned a Dr. phil. from the University of Salzburg and completed his Habilitation at the University of Heidelberg. He held positions at Heidelberg (2008, 2014) and became Professor at the University of Munich in 2017.

Rolf Alfred Stein was a scholar in Tibetology and sinology who studied at the Seminar for Oriental Languages, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at INALCO (1949–1951), EPHE (1951–1975), and the Collège de France (1965–1982).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Chödrak Tenphel.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who earned a doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. She held posts at Kurukshetra University (1961–1962), the University of Delhi (1963–1970), and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991, 1993).
Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology. His academic posts include Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong (both attested 1998).

Ronald E. Purser is an academic in religious studies and philosophy who studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1991–1997) and San Francisco State University (~1997).

Ronald Egan is a sinologist who completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1971–1977). He held appointments at Harvard (~1977–1985), the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1992–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

Ronald Eric Emmerick was a scholar of Iranian, Indological, and Tibetan studies who studied under Harold Walter Bailey and completed his PhD at Oxford. He served as a lecturer at SOAS (~1964–1971) and as professor at the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).

Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 1985 and held a post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005, 2014).
Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a post as Associate Professor in the Religious Studies Department at the University of Calgary (~1977, attested 2001).

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1980. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1987) and Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng was a scholar in sinology, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University from ~1922 to 1926 and held a post at Yenching University from ~1926 to 1941.

Rong Ma is a sociologist and Tibetologist who earned a doctorate in social geography at Brown University. He served as Director of the Institute of Sociology and Anthropology at Peking University (attested 1998).

Rongdao Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and was a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
